title: Bill of Materials — what a produced item is made of
description: A BOM is data an explosion walks, not a procedure someone remembers. quantity is the output the component list is stated for, so an explosion scales the component quantities by produced/quantity — which is why it is required and strictly positive rather than defaulted to one. A component that is itself produced (it has its own submitted BOM) is expanded further, and a BOM that transitively contains its own item is refused by name rather than looped over.

item.description: The item this bill produces. A component that names its own BOM's output item is a cycle, refused at explosion.

quantity.description: The output quantity the component list below is stated for.

rate.description: The finished item's valuation rate. Optional: the posting layer falls back to the item master's valuation_rate.

warehouse.description: The warehouse this component is issued from. A sub-assembly is produced into one warehouse and consumed from it, which is not always the warehouse its parent's other components come from — so the source is declared per component and the work order's from_warehouse is only the default.

components.description: The components consumed to produce `quantity` of `item`. At least one: a bill of materials that requires nothing is a declaration, not a recipe.

harvest: the BOM field surface (produced item, output quantity, component lines, component rate)
a bill of materials as data an explosion walks rather than a procedure
x-erp-provenance.note: Field and lifecycle shapes from the upstream BOM doctype, re-expressed as our own schema and workflow data. No upstream file was read into this repository; no upstream code, schema or text is copied.
